headline: High-risk write/conflict and cascading-error pathways exist; prompt-injection and leakage are lower but nonzero due to shared file-based workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero has no shared channel or ingestion surface by profile, while Plandex reads/writes project files and stdin/stdout. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or file handoff, so hijack risk is limited and not default. No evidence of MCP or clipboard bridging either agent.
conditions: IF an operator copies LightZero output into Plandex prompts or files, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF Plandex is run in auto-apply mode on copied content, malicious instructions can be acted on.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting raw model output into Plandex prompts.
Use a human review step before any apply action.
Strip instructions from any text transferred between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightZero touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network egress, while Plandex touches source code and can read/write the project directory. Leakage requires an unusual shared workspace or manual transfer, and the blast radius is typically source code rather than regulated data.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same project directory, Plandex can read files LightZero does not protect.
IF source code contains secrets and is copied into Plandex prompts, those secrets may be exposed to its model provider.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Remove secrets from source trees before handing them to Plandex.
Disable broad file sharing between tools.
Review any outbound prompts for sensitive content before sending.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero cannot write files, but Plandex can execute shell, write the filesystem, and modify git state. In a shared repo or workspace, Plandex's default write capabilities can conflict with other instances or external edits; uncertainty about orchestration locking pushes this to high rather than medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git checkout, Plandex can race with external edits.
IF multiple Plandex instances operate on the same backend state, write conflicts can corrupt plans or commits.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout.
Pause other writers before Plandex applies changes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightZero is a game-playing agent and Plandex is a coding agent with review-then-apply workflow. If LightZero output is treated as authoritative planning input, Plandex can propagate errors into code changes; the sandbox reduces but does not eliminate this because verification is not guaranteed by default.
conditions: IF LightZero-generated text is fed into Plandex as facts or requirements, Plandex may act on incorrect content.
IF Plandex auto-apply is enabled, unverified upstream errors can become filesystem changes.
mitigations: Require a human check before apply.
Mark LightZero output as untrusted input.
Ask Plandex to restate assumptions before editing.
Use small, isolated tasks when chaining outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data class, residency mismatch, or retention policy gap is evidenced in either profile. LightZero touches no data classes, and Plandex only lists source code and model-provider API keys; there is no documented PHI, EU PII, or residency constraint to violate.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into either agent, a separate compliance review is required.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools.
Document any data-class expansion before deployment.
Review vendor terms if secrets are added to Plandex workflows.
